answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation with a real cost to entry: every agent must lock a small deposit before it can earn, and that deposit is slashed when peers flag fake work. A hollow identity with no history and no stake earns nothing, so spinning up thousands of clones buys no influence. Reputation should grow slowly from verified, useful work and decay fast after abuse, so an attacker standing on the ledge of a fresh identity cannot reach the zenith of trust overnight. Sybil resistance comes from making each fake identity expensive while honest ones grow more valuable.
